chapter: Life in Columbus and recent activity
title: Visiting artists and the 'Ev' chart

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And we talked yesterday about Benny Carter having come in not so long ago to do a concert.

Benny Carter, backed him, then Clark Terry was in just last month, but of course I was sick at the time. And the time that he was here before which was a year ago, I didn't play with him then because he had his own charts and he did it with the jazz arts group, but Clark has been here twice. Then Phil Woods, I worked with him, Phil Woods, I worked with him and did a little seminar with him there in the school. Yeah, Louie Bellson was here last year.
You said that you had written a chart that he's interested in recording.
Well it's just a blues chart, blues chart. It's swinging, you know just one of those old gut bucket things and Louie likes it.
Great. What's the name of it?
'Ev.' Named after my wife. E V.
Just a little old simple thing that's swinging, you know, not too many notes but nice riffs.
Have you sent that to him yet?
Not as yet, I haven't copied it off. As I told you I had the score-transposed score, I've got to get it off now on paper, and I've got to get that all set, you know set up and send it to him.
Well that'll be something to look forward to.

Oh yeah, yeah. I like the idea of that and then Louie, see, I remember when Louie won the Gene Krupa contest in drumming. I was with Benny Goodman right there at the Paramount Theatre, and he was right up the street at Wurlitzer's there on 42nd Street, and that's where they held it and that's where he won it.
